examples.ko: 이 수업에서는 연역법과 귀납법의 차이를 배워요.
examples.en: In this class, we learn the difference between deduction and induction.
Most math proofs are worked out by deduction.

examples.ko: 연역법을 쓰면 결론이 더 분명하게 나와요.
examples.en: If you use deduction, the conclusion comes out more clearly.

examples.ko: 연역법은 큰 규칙에서 시작해서 결론을 찾아가요.
examples.en: Deduction starts from a big rule and works toward a conclusion.

examples.ko: 이 논문은 연역법에 따라 가설을 세웠어요.
examples.en: This paper set up its hypothesis according to the deductive method.

examples.ko: 연역법 문제가 시험에 나와서 많이 헤맸어요.
examples.en: A deduction question came up on the test, and I struggled a lot.

explain: 짝말은 '귀납법'이라서 보통 둘을 함께 비교해서 말해요. 일상 대화보다 논술, 철학, 수학 수업에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Its counterpart is '귀납법' (the inductive method), so the two are usually compared together. It appears more in essays, philosophy and math classes than in daily conversation.

examples.ko: 이 풍습의 연원은 아주 오래전으로 올라가요.
examples.en: The origin of this custom goes back a very long time.

examples.ko: 단어의 연원을 찾아보면 재미있는 이야기가 많아요.
examples.en: If you look up the origin of a word, there are many interesting stories.
The origin of this festival isn't even clear.

examples.ko: 그 축제의 연원에 대해서는 의견이 달라요.
examples.en: Opinions differ about the origin of that festival.

examples.ko: 이 말의 연원이 궁금해서 사전을 찾아봤어요.
examples.en: I was curious about the origin of this word, so I looked it up in a dictionary.

examples.ko: 전통 음식의 연원까지 설명해 주는 책이에요.
examples.en: It's a book that even explains the origins of traditional foods.

explain: '유래'나 '기원'과 비슷하지만 연원은 글이나 발표에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 보통 '연원이 깊다', '연원을 찾다'처럼 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '유래'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It is similar to '유래' and '기원', but 연원 is a stiffer word used in writing and presentations. It usually appears as '연원이 깊다' or '연원을 찾다'. In everyday talk, '유래' sounds more natural.

examples.en: This savings account has an annual interest rate of 3 percent.
Check the annual interest rate before you take out a loan.
The annual interest rate differs a little from bank to bank.
If you deposit 1 million won at 5 percent a year, you get 50,000 won in a year.
A card loan has a high annual rate, and there are fees too.
I compared annual interest rates and then opened an account.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '금리'나 '이자'라고 더 많이 말해요. 은행 상품 설명이나 계약서에서 '연 3%'처럼 숫자와 함께 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In daily conversation people more often say '금리' or '이자'. 연이율 appears in bank product descriptions and contracts, usually alongside numbers like '연 3%'.

examples.ko: 그는 요즘 신문에 연재소설을 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: These days he is writing a serial novel for a newspaper.

examples.ko: 이 연재소설은 매주 금요일에 새 편이 올라와요.
examples.en: A new installment of this serial novel is posted every Friday.
The serial novel became popular and was published as a book.
It started as a web serial and even became a drama.

examples.ko: 연재소설 다음 편이 너무 궁금해서 잠이 안 와요.
examples.en: I'm so curious about the next installment of the serial novel that I can't sleep.
The author is busy because she is tied up with her serial novel.

explain: '연재하다', '연재되다'와 짝으로 자주 써요. 신문, 잡지, 인터넷 어디에서 나오든 한 편씩 나눠 싣는 소설이면 연재소설이라고 해요. 온라인 소설은 '웹소설'이라고도 많이 불러요.
explain_en: It pairs naturally with '연재하다' and '연재되다'. Whether it runs in a newspaper, a magazine or online, a novel published in installments is a 연재소설. Online ones are also often called '웹소설'.

en: successive victories; a series of wins

examples.ko: 우리 팀이 올해 연전연승을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is keeping up a winning streak this year.
That player won the tournament with win after win.
A reporter asked what the secret to the winning streak was.
The winning streak has finally come to an end.
At first it was win after win, but we lost the last game.
Don't just hope for win after win; enjoy it while you play.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '연전연패'예요. 스포츠 뉴스나 게임 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '연승'만 써도 통하지만 연전연승은 싸울 때마다 이긴다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '연전연패' (a string of losses). It shows up often in sports news and talk about games. '연승' alone also works, but 연전연승 feels stronger, as if the team wins every time it plays.

examples.en: That team won game after game last year and took the title.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에서 우리 학교가 연전연승하고 있어요.
examples.en: Our school is winning one match after another in this tournament.
The player who had been winning every match suddenly got injured.
I envy my friend who keeps winning game after game.
We won every match at first, but lost in the final.
Even if you keep winning, you must not let your guard down.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '연전연패하다'예요. 보통 대화에서는 '계속 이기다'라고 더 쉽게 말하고, 연전연승하다는 뉴스나 해설처럼 조금 힘주어 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '연전연패하다'. In casual talk people more simply say '계속 이기다'; 연전연승하다 suits news and commentary, where you want a more emphatic tone.

examples.en: Squid and clams are mollusks.
We learned the features of mollusks in science class.
Snails also belong to the mollusks.
Mollusks have no bones and soft bodies.

examples.ko: 시험에 연체동물과 절지동물을 구별하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The test had a question on telling mollusks from arthropods.

examples.ko: 연체동물 중에는 껍데기가 있는 것도 있고 없는 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Among mollusks, some have shells and some don't.

explain: 학교 과학 수업에서 쓰는 분류 이름이에요. 일상 대화에서는 오징어, 조개, 달팽이처럼 구체적인 이름으로 말해요. 같은 계열의 분류 이름으로 '절지동물', '척추동물'도 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a classification name used in school science. In daily talk people name the animals themselves, such as squid, clams or snails. Related classification terms worth knowing are '절지동물' and '척추동물'.

examples.ko: 열대림에는 신기한 동물이 아주 많이 살아요.
examples.en: Many amazing animals live in tropical forests.
I'm worried because tropical forests are disappearing fast.
I took part in an activity to protect tropical forests in Brazil.

examples.ko: 열대림은 일 년 내내 날씨가 더워요.
examples.en: In tropical forests, the weather is hot all year round.
The photographer spent a week in a tropical forest.

examples.ko: 열대림의 나무를 함부로 베면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut down trees in the tropical forest carelessly.

explain: '열대우림'과 비슷한 자리에서 자주 만나는 말이에요. 환경 뉴스에서 '열대림 파괴'처럼 많이 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '밀림'이나 '정글'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: You often meet it in the same contexts as '열대우림' (tropical rainforest). Environmental news uses phrases like '열대림 파괴' (destruction of tropical forests), and in daily talk people also say '밀림' or '정글'.

examples.ko: 그는 학벌에 대한 열등의식이 있다고 해요.
examples.en: They say he has a sense of inferiority about his educational background.

examples.ko: 열등의식은 남과 비교할 때 더 커져요.
examples.en: A sense of inferiority grows bigger when you compare yourself with others.
I started working out to get free of my sense of inferiority.

examples.ko: 열등의식 때문에 사람들 앞에서 말하기가 힘들어요.
examples.en: Because of my feelings of inferiority, it's hard to speak in front of people.

examples.ko: 아이에게 열등의식을 심어 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't plant a sense of inferiority in a child.

examples.ko: 열등의식도 잘 쓰면 노력하는 힘이 돼요.
examples.en: Even a sense of inferiority can become a driving force if used well.

explain: 일상에서는 '열등감'이 더 자주 들리고, 열등의식은 설명하거나 글로 쓸 때 어울려요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '우월감'이에요. '콤플렉스가 있다'도 비슷한 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
explain_en: In everyday speech '열등감' is heard more often; 열등의식 suits explanations and writing. The opposite feeling is '우월감'. Koreans also say '콤플렉스가 있다' with a similar meaning.

examples.en: The teacher banged on the desk and spoke with fiery passion.

examples.ko: 그의 열변에 사람들이 모두 귀를 기울였어요.
examples.en: Everyone listened closely to his passionate speech.
When the fiery speech ended, applause broke out.
I even spoke with all my passion, but nobody was persuaded.

examples.ko: 그 연설가의 열변은 지금도 기억에 남아요.
examples.en: That speaker's fiery speech still stays in my memory.
He moved people's hearts with his passionate speech.

explain: 거의 '열변을 토하다'의 모양으로 써요. 그냥 '열심히 말하다'보다 목소리와 몸짓에 힘이 들어간 강한 말하기를 나타내요. 연설, 토론, 강의 같은 상황에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 그는 환경 보호의 중요성에 대해 열변을 토했어요.
phrases.en: He spoke passionately about the importance of protecting the environment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토하다'가 말을 쏟아낸다는 뜻으로 쓰여요. 열정을 담아 길고 힘 있게 주장하는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Here '토하다' means pouring words out. It describes arguing at length and with force and passion.

explain_en: It is almost always used in the form '열변을 토하다'. It is stronger than simply speaking hard, since voice and gestures are full of force. It fits speeches, debates and lectures.

examples.en: He threw the window wide open.
Every morning I fling the curtains open and air out the room.

examples.ko: 누가 갑자기 문을 열어젖혀서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Someone suddenly threw the door open and I was startled.

examples.ko: 방문을 열어젖히자 찬 바람이 훅 들어왔어요.
examples.en: When I threw the bedroom door open, a cold wind rushed in.

examples.ko: 동생이 서랍을 열어젖히며 뭘 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is yanking drawers open, looking for something.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 창을 열어젖힌 채 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: I was angry and shouted with the window thrown wide open.

explain: 그냥 '열다'보다 거침없이 확 여는 느낌이 있어요. 문, 창문, 커튼처럼 큰 것을 '활짝' 여는 상황에 잘 어울려요. 조심스럽게 여는 장면에는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Compared with plain '열다', it has a bold, sweeping feel of opening something all at once. It fits big things like doors, windows and curtains, often with '활짝'. You wouldn't use it for opening something carefully.

en: being excused; exemption (from a group activity)

examples.en: Anyone who is injured is excused from today's training.

examples.ko: 저는 감기 때문에 체육 시간에 열외가 됐어요.
examples.en: Because of a cold, I was excused from P.E. class.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 그 사람만 열외로 두기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to leave only that person out of our team.
Nobody is excused from the cleaning this time.

examples.ko: 열외 없이 모두 회의에 참석해야 해요.
examples.en: Everyone must attend the meeting, with no exceptions.

examples.ko: 단체 사진에서 나만 열외인 것 같아 속상했어요.
examples.en: I felt upset, as if I were the only one left out of the group photo.

explain: '예외'와 비슷하지만 열외는 훈련, 청소, 모임 같은 단체 활동에서 빠지는 사람에게 써요. '열외 없이'로 모두 참여해야 한다고 말하는 경우가 많아요. 군대에서 많이 쓰는 말이라 조금 딱딱하게 들릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is close to '예외' (exception), but 열외 is for someone excused from group activities such as training, cleaning or meetings. People often say '열외 없이' to mean everyone takes part. It is widely used in the military, so it can sound a bit stiff.

examples.en: A story about the two actors' romance appeared in the news.

examples.ko: 그 정치인은 젊은 시절 염문을 뿌렸다고 해요.
examples.en: They say that politician was rumored to have many romances in his youth.
The singer caught up in a romance rumor held a press conference.
The two strongly denied the rumors of a romance.
The romance rumor spread quickly.

examples.ko: 그 영화감독은 염문 때문에 한동안 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: That film director couldn't work for a while because of a romance scandal.

explain: 외래어 '스캔들'과 달리 연애나 사랑에 관한 소문에만 써요. 주로 연예인이나 유명인 기사에서 보는 글말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '연애설'이라고 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 젊을 때 여러 사람과 염문을 뿌렸어요.
phrases.en: That actor was linked romantically with many people when he was young.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번이 아니라 여러 사람과 연애 소문이 난다는 느낌이 있어요. 뉴스나 이야기에서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suggests romance rumors with several people, not just once. It is used in news and storytelling.
phrases.en_equiv: be rumored to have many romances

explain_en: Unlike the loanword '스캔들', it is used only for rumors about romance. It is mostly written language seen in articles about celebrities, and in conversation people often say '연애설'.

examples.ko: 그는 성격이 염세적이라 늘 세상을 어둡게 봐요.
examples.en: He is world-weary by nature, so he always sees the world as dark.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 전체적으로 염세적 분위기가 강해요.
examples.en: This novel has a strongly pessimistic mood overall.

examples.ko: 요즘 뉴스를 너무 봐서 염세적으로 변했어요.
examples.en: I watched too much news lately and became cynical about the world.
When I read a gloomy, world-weary poem, my mood sinks.
My brother used to be world-weary, but he brightened up after finding a hobby.
Even people who aren't world-weary get tired sometimes.

explain: '비관적'은 앞일을 어둡게 보는 것이고, 염세적은 세상이나 삶 자체에 싫증을 느끼는 쪽이에요. 반대말로는 '낙천적'을 써요. '염세적인', '염세적으로'처럼 뒤에 말을 붙여 써요.
explain_en: '비관적' means seeing the future in a dark light, while 염세적 is weariness with the world or life itself. Its opposite is '낙천적'. It is used with endings like '염세적인' and '염세적으로'.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 소설에는 염세주의가 짙게 깔려 있어요.
examples.en: Pessimism runs thick through that author's novels.

examples.ko: 염세주의로 흐르지 않도록 좋은 사람들을 만나요.
examples.en: I meet good people so that I don't drift into pessimism.
I gave a presentation on pessimism in philosophy class.
Pessimism is the opposite way of thinking from optimism.
He talks like a pessimist, but he is actually kind.
This song expresses pessimism through humor.

explain: 철학이나 문학 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '염세적이다'나 '비관적이다'처럼 풀어서 말해요. 반대말은 '낙관주의'예요.
explain_en: It is a stiff word for philosophy and literature talk. In daily life people say things like '염세적이다' or '비관적이다' instead. The opposite is '낙관주의'.

examples.ko: 돼지 염통을 볶아서 먹어 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever tried stir-fried pig heart?

examples.ko: 닭 염통은 쫄깃해서 꼬치로 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Chicken hearts are chewy and taste good on skewers.
My grandmother calls the heart by the old word 'yeomtong'.
We made a stir-fry with beef heart.
Please give me one geun of heart at the butcher shop.

examples.ko: 옛날 소설에는 염통이라는 말이 가끔 나와요.
examples.en: The word 'yeomtong' sometimes appears in old novels.

explain: '심장'의 우리말이지만 지금은 몸 이야기에서는 '심장'을 써요. 염통은 돼지, 닭, 소의 내장 부위를 말하는 음식 이야기나 어르신들의 말에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It is the native Korean word for 심장 (heart), but in talk about the body people now use '심장'. 염통 is mostly heard when talking about the heart of a pig, chicken or cow as food, or in the speech of older people.

examples.en: A bizarre photo became a hot topic online.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 내용이 너무 엽기적이라 보기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The story of that movie was so freakish that it was hard to watch.
I tried a ridiculously spicy ramen.

examples.ko: 내 친구는 엽기적일 만큼 장난을 좋아해요.
examples.en: My friend likes pranks to an outrageous degree.
That comic is fun because of its wild, bizarre ideas.
I like stories that are funny without being bizarre.

explain: 평범한 범위에서 한참 벗어나 기괴하고 별난 것에 써요. 음식이나 유머 이야기에서는 장난스럽게 '황당할 만큼 독특한'이라는 느낌이고, 진지한 이야기에서는 불쾌하고 기이하다는 느낌이 강해요. 듣는 사람이 불편할 수 있으니 상황을 보고 쓰세요.
explain_en: It describes something far outside the ordinary, strange and grotesque. About food or humor it can be playful, meaning outrageously unusual; in serious contexts it feels unpleasant and weird. Because it may make listeners uncomfortable, use it with care.

examples.en: I think there is no eternally unchanging truth in the world.
Trends don't stay fixed forever; they keep changing.

examples.ko: 법도 영구불변은 아니라서 시대에 따라 고쳐요.
examples.en: Laws are not fixed forever either, so they are revised over time.
It's hard to find anything truly eternal in reality.
Even things that seem unchanging will change someday.
No system remains unchanged forever.

explain: 한자어 네 글자라서 글이나 연설, 토론에서 주로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '변하지 않는'이라고 풀어서 말해요. '영구불변의 진리'처럼 쓰거나, '영구불변은 없다'처럼 부정하는 문장에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: As a four-character Sino-Korean word, it mostly appears in writing, speeches and debates. In daily talk people say '변하지 않는' instead. It is used in phrases like '영구불변의 진리' or in negations such as '영구불변은 없다'.

examples.en: This document has to be kept permanently.

examples.ko: 사고로 시력을 영구히 잃을 수도 있대요.
examples.en: They say you could permanently lose your eyesight in an accident.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 영구히 문을 닫기로 했어요.
examples.en: That shop decided to close for good.
This promise will be kept forever.

examples.ko: 사진을 영구히 남기고 싶어서 액자에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I wanted to keep the photo permanently, so I put it in a frame.

examples.ko: 영구히 사용할 수 있는 이용권을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pass that can be used permanently.

explain: '영원히'와 비슷하지만 영구히는 보관, 정지, 권리, 규칙처럼 딱딱한 사무적인 이야기에 어울려요. 사랑이나 이별 같은 감정을 말할 때는 '영원히'가 더 자연스러워요. 반대되는 말은 '일시적으로'예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '영원히', but 영구히 fits formal, practical topics such as storage, suspension, rights and rules. For feelings like love or parting, '영원히' sounds more natural. The opposite is '일시적으로' (temporarily).

examples.en: When autumn came, the rice ripened.

examples.ko: 포도가 알알이 영글어서 곧 따도 되겠어요.
examples.en: The grapes have ripened one by one, so we can pick them soon.

examples.ko: 오랜 준비 끝에 우리의 꿈도 영글고 있어요.
examples.en: After long preparation, our dream is also taking shape.

examples.ko: 사과가 영글 때까지 조금만 더 기다려요.
examples.en: Let's wait a little longer until the apples ripen.
You can harvest only after the grains are full and ripe.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 사랑이 천천히 영글어 가요.
examples.en: The love between the two is slowly ripening.

explain: '익다'와 달리 영글다는 곡식이나 열매의 알이 속까지 꽉 차는 것을 말해서 음식이 익는 데는 쓰지 않아요. 꿈, 사랑, 생각이 무르익을 때도 비유로 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져 '영근 열매'처럼 활용해요.
explain_en: Unlike '익다', 영글다 is about the grains or fruit filling out fully, so it is not used for food being cooked. It is also used figuratively for dreams, love or ideas maturing. The ㄹ drops in forms like '영근 열매'.

examples.en: After graduating from university, he started farming.
There is a program that supports successors to family farms.
I took out a loan for the funds needed for farming.

examples.ko: 영농은 날씨에 따라 수확이 크게 달라져요.
examples.en: In farming, the harvest changes a lot depending on the weather.
Farmers gathered to learn new farming methods.
She paid for her children's education with money earned from farming.

explain: 일상에서 농사짓는 일은 보통 '농사'라고 해요. 영농은 '영농 조합', '영농 후계자', '영농 자금'처럼 제도나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: In daily life, working the land is usually called '농사'. 영농 appears in institutional or news contexts, such as '영농 조합', '영농 후계자' and '영농 자금'.

examples.ko: 저 사람 뒷모습이 영락없이 우리 아버지예요.
examples.en: That person's back view is exactly like my father's.
Her smile is the spitting image of my mother.
If we leave this late, we'll definitely be late.
In that hat, you look just like a tourist.

examples.ko: 그 말투는 영락없이 형이 하던 말투예요.
examples.en: That way of speaking is exactly how my older brother used to talk.

examples.ko: 비가 오는데 우산이 없으면 영락없이 젖어요.
examples.en: If it's raining and you have no umbrella, you'll surely get wet.

explain: '영락없이'나 '영락없는'의 모양으로 자주 써요. 닮았다고 말할 때 '영락없는 아버지'처럼 쓰거나, 안 좋은 일이 틀림없이 생길 때 '영락없이 늦어요'처럼 말해요. '똑같다', '틀림없다'보다 확신하는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly used in the forms '영락없이' and '영락없는'. You say '영락없는 아버지' for a strong resemblance, or '영락없이 늦어요' when something bad is bound to happen. It sounds more certain than '똑같다' or '틀림없다'.

examples.ko: 학교 강당에서 영사기로 영화를 틀어 줬어요.
examples.en: They played a movie with a projector in the school hall.
The sound of an old projector running feels warm and nostalgic.

examples.ko: 영사기 불빛이 어두운 극장 벽에 번졌어요.
examples.en: The projector light spread across the wall of the dark theater.
I looked at an old projector at the museum.

examples.ko: 영사기는 필름을 한 장씩 빠르게 비춰요.
examples.en: A projector shines film frames one after another very quickly.

examples.ko: 영사기에 필름을 거는 일을 아저씨가 맡았어요.
examples.en: The man took charge of loading the film onto the projector.

explain: 극장이나 옛날 학교에서 필름 영화를 비추는 기계를 떠올리는 말이에요. 요즘 회의나 수업에서 화면을 비추는 기기는 보통 '프로젝터'나 '빔프로젝터'라고 해요.
explain_en: It brings to mind the machine that shows film movies in theaters or old schools. For the device used in meetings or classes today, people usually say '프로젝터' or '빔프로젝터'.

examples.en: The visuals of this movie are really outstanding.

examples.ko: 영상미 덕분에 줄거리가 약해도 지루하지 않았어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the beautiful visuals, it wasn't boring even though the plot was weak.
They say the director paid a lot of attention to the visual beauty.
The visuals were good, but the story was a bit disappointing.
There are many comments praising the drama's visuals.
It's a documentary famous for its beautiful nature visuals.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 광고, 다큐처럼 화면 연출이 아름다울 때 칭찬으로 써요. '영상미는 좋은데 스토리가…'처럼 이야기나 연기와 따로 떼어 평가할 때 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is a compliment for beautiful on-screen visuals in movies, dramas, ads and documentaries. People often judge it separately from the story or acting, as in '영상미는 좋은데 스토리가…'.

examples.ko: 코로나 때 영세업자들이 큰 어려움을 겪었어요.
examples.en: During COVID, small business owners went through great hardship.
The government announced a subsidy to help small business owners.
Small business owners struggle to hold on when the rent goes up.

examples.ko: 저희 부모님도 작은 가게를 하는 영세업자예요.
examples.en: My parents are also small business owners running a little shop.

examples.ko: 영세업자에게는 세금을 줄여 주는 제도가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a system that reduces taxes for small business owners.

examples.ko: 대기업과 영세업자 사이의 거래가 공정해야 해요.
examples.en: Deals between big companies and small business owners need to be fair.

explain: 뉴스나 정책 이야기에서 쓰는 말이에요. 규모가 작고 형편이 넉넉하지 않다는 느낌이 있어서, 직접 말할 때는 '자영업자'나 '소상공인'이 더 부드러워요.
explain_en: It is a word from news and policy discussions, carrying the sense of a small, financially tight business. In direct conversation, '자영업자' or '소상공인' sounds softer.
